title: 2019 SDNY Indictment (19 Cr. 490)
summary: United States v. Jeffrey Epstein: conspiracy to commit sex trafficking of minors (§371) and sex trafficking of minors (§1591), alleging conduct 2002–2005 in New York and Palm Beach — girls as young as 14 enticed to 'massages' escalating to sex acts for cash, victims recruited to recruit others. Epstein was found dead August 10, 2019 (suicide, per the NYC medical examiner); the criminal case abated. Guilt was never adjudicated.
tldr: The unsealed 2019 SDNY indictment charged Epstein with sex trafficking of minors and conspiracy, alleging he exploited dozens of girls as young as 14 at his Manhattan and Palm Beach homes from 2002 to 2005; the case was dismissed after his death.
ai_summary:
AI review of the full indictment (19 Cr. 490), read in full:
- Counts: Count One — sex trafficking conspiracy (18 U.S.C. § 371); Count Two — sex trafficking of minors (18 U.S.C. § 1591(a), (b)(2)).
- Alleged conduct, 2002–2005: Epstein enticed and recruited minor girls to his Manhattan mansion and Palm Beach estate to engage in sex acts, paying hundreds of dollars in cash per encounter; victims were recruited for 'massages' that escalated sexually, and victims were paid hundreds of dollars to recruit additional girls, creating 'a vast network of underage victims.'
- Victims were 'as young as 14 years old'; Epstein 'intentionally sought out minors and knew that many of his victims were in fact under the age of 18, including because, in some instances, minor victims expressly told him their age.'
- Overt acts name three minor victims and three employees who scheduled encounters; forfeiture sought for 9 East 71st Street, New York.
- SDNY's case page confirms: charges unsealed July 8, 2019; case dismissed via nolle prosequi on August 29, 2019 following the defendant's death. Guilt was never adjudicated.
- Note: the 'suicide per the NYC medical examiner' detail in the record summary is outside the indictment itself and was not in the text reviewed.
- Record summary otherwise verified accurate against the document.
